newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to spend $2 bln in power in next 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to spend $2 bln in power in next 10 yrs.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to spend around $2 billion to build new power plants in the next 10 years and will rely heavily on coal to meet future energy needs, a state power utility official said on Thursday.
The Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) will build only one new hydroelectric plant under its generation plan to add almost 700 megawatts of power to the national grid by 2002, he said.
Remaining energy needs will be met by diesel, gas turbine, combined cycle and coal power plants, he added.
"In the next 10 years we'll need something like $2 billion in investment to build new power plants," he said.

The CEB plans to build two or more diesel plants supplying 90 megawatts (MW) by 1998, combined cycle plants (gas and steam turbines) providing 300 MW by 1999 and two 150 MW coal plants by 2002, the official said.
"It will be all coal thereafter unless we go for nuclear power which is unlikely as the country is too small," he said. "We plan to build up to 900 MW of coal power plants by 2006."
The Indian Ocean island has a power generating capacity of about 1,250 MW, 84 percent of which come from hydroelectric plants and the balance from thermal plants.
The CEB will go ahead with plans to build a 70 MW hydroelectric plant in the central hills but has shelved a 150 MW hydropower plant for environmental reasons, he said.
Sri Lanka faced a severe power crisis earlier this year, with daily power cuts of up to eight hours, after monsoon rains failed.
The power crunch was attributed to delays in building new power plants to meet rising demand.
